title: A tool is an action. A skill is a workflow.
body: An MCP connection exposes capabilities. A skill teaches an agent when and how to use them. Installing either is not evidence that an operation works.

title: Prefer the route that stays out of the way.
body: Use a connector, CLI or native test before screen control. Reserve the interface for visual judgment and the specific steps programmatic routes cannot complete.

title: Prove one small, real operation.
body: A native fixture built and ran. A browser assertion passed. A GPU rendered a frame. These narrow checks said more than a long list of installed applications.

title: Keep credentials out of the conversation.
body: Reuse protected credentials inside approved background workers. Check real API access without exposing tokens, broadening Keychain access or treating a permission dialog as automation.

title: Fail before the expensive work starts.
body: Gitleaks and targeted Ruff checks now precede project commands in the local validator. A synthetic secret and a Python error both stopped the path as expected.

title: A finding can be a test fixture.
body: A synthetic token surfaced in generated Python bytecode. Generating the fixture at runtime kept the test realistic without adding a broad scanner exclusion.

title: Let the evidence keep growing.
body: Safe tool receipts and reviewed kit revisions become part of this field guide. Uninstrumented calls and stale sources remain explicit gaps, not invented coverage.
